answers.text: I would tell it to always give three lines in this order: drop-off time, pallet count, then any damage noted. The time should just be the time, the pallet count just the number, and the damage line says what was damaged or 'none' if nothing was said.
I would say list every call with the time, customer, topic and what happened, in that order, and then say how many need a follow-up call.
Something about the timing in this note doesn't sit right with me, I would want another look at it before it's filed.
9 late out of 118, that's close to what they wrote, about 92%.
I would go with the second one, it just looks more careful, with all the numbers written out.
I would send Email 2, the one with the actual volume numbers and the PO log reference.
1. No, wait until the tool's approved. 2. Yes, that's aggregate. 3. No, that budget hasn't been signed off. 4. No, I wouldn't risk it. 5. No, that's personal, someone's home address.
This one has the rates, the NDA bit, and what work is included. I would just write up a short summary of it for the file, covering all of that.
I would check the stock totals in the summary against the actual warehouse counts before it goes out.
The step where it reads the invoice and pulls out the numbers is the one I'd watch most, because everything after depends on that being right.
